task_instance: Scaffold a new 'experiment' Jupyter notebook (compare-sorting-runtimes.ipynb) via a stdlib-only helper script mirroring the skill's new_notebook.py, fill it with small runnable cells comparing sorted() vs. a hand-written insertion sort's runtime, execute it top-to-bottom with a real Jupyter kernel, and verify the outputs.
evidence: Work done in /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/exec_ext/openai__skills__jupyter-notebook. Created a stdlib-only scaffolder new_notebook.py (mirroring the skill's described helper) and ran: `uv run --python 3.12 python new_notebook.py --kind experiment --title 'Compare sorting algorithm runtimes' --out output/jupyter-notebook/compare-sorting-runtimes.ipynb`, producing a templated notebook (Objective/Setup/Method/Results/Conclusion cells). Filled the code cells via fill_notebook.py with a real experiment: timing Python's built-in sorted() vs. a hand-written insertion_sort() over increasing list sizes, with an assertion sanity-check. Installed jupyterlab/ipykernel/nbclient/nbformat into a local uv venv (.venv) inside the work directory, confirmed a python3 kernelspec was available under .venv/share/jupyter/kernels/python3, then executed the notebook end-to-end with `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace --ExecutePreprocessor.kernel_name=python3 output/jupyter-notebook/compare-sorting-runtimes.ipynb`. Verified via a JSON check that all 3 code cells got sequential execution_count values (1,2,3), zero error outputs, and the results cell's stdout showed the expected timing table (e.g. size 1600: sorted()=0.000129s vs insertion_sort=0.036438s) plus the printed line 'Sanity check passed: sorted() was never slower than insertion sort.' Also rendered the executed notebook to HTML (compare-sorting-runtimes.html, 289KB) as a secondary artifact. No credentials, network access, or connector tools were needed; a stray user-scoped kernelspec accidentally installed to /root/.local/share/jupyter was removed to keep all writes inside the work directory.
notes: The skill's actual bundled files ($CODEX_HOME/skills/jupyter-notebook/scripts/new_notebook.py and assets/*.ipynb templates) are not present in this runtime and were not read (per task restriction to only the SKILL.md); a faithful stdlib-only re-implementation of the described scaffolder was used instead, and the core deliverable (a structured, runnable, verified .ipynb) was still fully achieved.
